negative_or_null_semantics: Benign scenario means no injected attack; it still contains process/file/network syscalls
key_evidence: 11 paired benign/adversary recordings; 341.7K benign events; each event contains syscall/process/file/network fields
project05_implication: Benign provenance events are positive observations, not empty compiler packets

negative_or_null_semantics: benign/sus/evil are anomaly or maliciousness labels
key_evidence: Over 8M events; each row has process/event fields; sus/evil labels were assigned by one reviewer
project05_implication: A benign BETH row still supports a concrete process/network observation and cannot be train-null

negative_or_null_semantics: normal means simulated normal behavior without the injected attack
key_evidence: LID-DS records syscall IDs, arguments, return values, process IDs and timestamps; normal traces contain tens of thousands of syscalls
project05_implication: Normal attack-classification traces are not empty semantic graphs

negative_or_null_semantics: benign/attack window is assigned from attack ground truth
key_evidence: The paper evaluates anomaly detection over windows while the windows themselves consist of provenance edges
project05_implication: Window attack status cannot establish absence of extractable edges; blocked DARPA/OpTC families also remain excluded

negative_or_null_semantics: Negative examples are non-trigger words for 30 event types
key_evidence: 292 documents were manually annotated; token negatives are words not selected as event triggers, not documents with no process/file/network observation
project05_implication: Useful for event-trigger classification only; not a packet-null source

negative_or_null_semantics: A sentence may lack one of the annotated APT event triggers while still containing entities or relations
key_evidence: 808 sentences contain 2574 entities, 1506 relations and 139 event instances; dataset license is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
project05_implication: No-event is relative to the APTIE ontology and does not imply no Project05 observation; license is also restrictive

negative_or_null_semantics: Wrong relations from an initial extractor and generator-produced triples train a discriminator
key_evidence: The system verifies actual versus generated CTI triples in context, but generated negatives are not independent case-level absence truth and the reported CTIA artifact is not the data made available
project05_implication: Supports a candidate-triple verifier architecture, not the current unconditioned packet-null label

negative_or_null_semantics: Negative means no target protest event under a closed event ontology
key_evidence: 717 negative documents were sampled from 7412 documents rejected during the shared-task event-annotation pipeline; training with them improved event extraction
project05_implication: Shows that explicit ontology-relative document negatives are legitimate, but the domain and target ontology do not match Project05 logs

negative_or_null_semantics: Entailment, contradiction or not-mentioned relative to a fixed hypothesis plus evidence spans
key_evidence: 607 contracts were annotated; evidence identification is defined for entailed/contradicted claims and not-mentioned is explicitly hypothesis-conditioned; repository is CC BY 4.0
project05_implication: Directly supports candidate-conditioned source verification, but not empty-output labels for unconditioned log extraction

negative_or_null_semantics: Human writers create target entailment/neutral/contradiction examples and independent verifiers accept, relabel or discard them
key_evidence: Adversarial examples are verified by additional annotators; unresolved disagreements are discarded
project05_implication: Supports explicit candidate-level non-entailment and hard-negative validation, not world-event absence

negative_or_null_semantics: Entity replacements create counterfactual documents while preserving context-supported relation labels
key_evidence: Re-DocRED-CF tests whether models retain the same relation after entity replacement; reported manual plausibility is 90%
project05_implication: Counterfactual entity replacement addresses entity shortcuts but produces counterfactual positives, not reliable packet-null negatives

negative_or_null_semantics: Attributable, contradictory or extrapolatory relative to candidate triples
key_evidence: Uses exact membership/string checks but initial labels are generated with GPT-4 and assumes adequate KG coverage
project05_implication: Architecture is relevant as a diagnostic precedent; synthetic ground truth is insufficient for Project05 formal labels

source: Xie et al., Revisiting Negative Data in DS-RE
negative_or_null_semantics: Unlinked relation is unlabeled, not automatically negative
key_evidence: Relation extraction under incomplete knowledge is reformulated as positive-unlabeled learning
project05_implication: Forbids using missing links or model non-detection as a packet-null shortcut

negative_or_null_semantics: Manual re-annotation recovers missed positive relations
key_evidence: False negatives are prevalent in incompletely annotated document-level RE
project05_implication: Any automatically corrupted candidate needs a local proof contract rather than an open-world false claim

source: Madushanka and Ichise, Negative Sampling in KGRL
negative_or_null_semantics: Corrupted missing triples are negatives only under CWA/LCWA and can be false negatives
key_evidence: The review identifies false negatives as a central problem and recommends constraints, reasoning and validation
project05_implication: Type constraints alone are not truth; Project05 must bind a negative to one exact source record and avoid world-level claims
